memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Israel had finished killing all the men of Ai in the fields and in the wilderness where they had chased them, and when every one of them had been put to the sword, all the Israelites returned to Ai and killed those who were in it. Twelve thousand men and women fell that day — all the people of Ai. For Joshua did not draw back the hand that held out his javelin until he had destroyed all who lived in Ai. — Josh 8:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a difficult account of complete judgment, and we do not soften it. As with Jericho, we understand it as a unique moment of divine judgment on the Canaanite nations in redemptive history, carried out through Israel — not a template for warfare or for how believers treat others today. We let the severity remind us of the deadly seriousness of sin and the holiness of God, and we resolve it, as Scripture teaches us to, in the light of Christ (Heb 1:1-2).

Amid the difficulty, one detail stands out for our reflection: "Joshua did not draw back the hand that held out his javelin until he had destroyed all who lived in Ai." Joshua held his position, his hand outstretched, until the work God had given was fully complete. He did not lower his hand halfway. He persevered to the end.

There is a principle of faithful perseverance here that we can carry into our own lives. It is easy to begin a task God gives us; it is much harder to see it through to completion. Joshua's steady, unwavering hand pictures the endurance God calls us to — not giving up partway, but finishing what He sets before us.

We serve One who perfectly finished the work the Father gave Him. On the cross, Jesus did not "draw back His hand" but endured to the very end, until He could say, "It is finished" (John 19:30). Because our Saviour finished His work completely, our salvation is secure and complete. And His example calls us to persevere in the good He has given us to do, trusting Him to carry us through to the end (Phil 1:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something God has called you to that you are tempted to leave unfinished?
2. What helps you persevere to the end rather than giving up partway?
3. How does Christ's finished work on the cross give you security and courage?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me endurance to finish what You give me to do. Thank You that Christ finished His saving work completely, and that You will carry me through to the end. Amen.
